statsPage.taxTipsSubtitle: Practical ways to reduce your tax burden
statsPage.tipKR0Desc: If annual sales are under 80M KRW, register as a simplified taxpayer to reduce VAT burden. Simplified rates (1.5%–4%) are much lower than the standard 10%.
statsPage.tipKR1Desc: Keep receipts for materials, shipping, booth rental, transportation, etc. Proper documentation allows expense deduction and reduces income tax.
statsPage.tipKR2Desc: Register your business card on HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) for automatic expense tracking from card transactions, simplifying bookkeeping.
statsPage.tipKR3Desc: Getting tax invoices from suppliers allows you to claim VAT input credits, effectively reducing your tax burden.
statsPage.tipKR4Desc: Small businesses with annual sales under 80M KRW may receive a reduction on simplified VAT payments.
statsPage.tipKR5Desc: Filing comprehensive income tax electronically via HomeTax grants a ₩20,000 tax credit.
statsPage.tipJP0Desc: Choosing blue return filing and submitting via e-Tax can grant up to ¥650,000 in deductions. Accurate bookkeeping is required.
statsPage.tipJP1Desc: Registering as a qualified invoice issuer allows your business partners to claim input tax credits, making transactions more favorable.
statsPage.tipJP2Desc: If taxable sales are under ¥10M, you can become a consumption tax-exempt business. Note the relationship with the invoice system.
statsPage.tipJP3Desc: Carefully record materials, booth fees, transportation, and communication costs as expenses. Receipts must be kept for 5 years.
statsPage.tipJP4Desc: File all applicable deductions—medical expenses, donations, life insurance premiums—to reduce your tax burden.
statsPage.tipUS0Desc: You can deduct half of your self-employment tax (15.3%) from AGI, effectively reducing your income tax burden.
statsPage.tipUS1Desc: If using a dedicated business space, deduct $5/sqft (max 300sqft) with the simplified method, or actual expenses.
statsPage.tipUS2Desc: Pay quarterly estimated taxes (Form 1040-ES) to avoid underpayment penalties. Due dates: 4/15, 6/15, 9/15, 1/15.
statsPage.tipUS3Desc: Keep receipts for materials, shipping, booth fees, and travel. Accounting software like QuickBooks or Wave makes this easier.
statsPage.tipUS4Desc: If selling in multiple states, check if you have sales tax collection/remittance obligations ("nexus") based on economic activity.
statsPage.tipGB0Desc: If VAT taxable turnover is under £150,000, the Flat Rate Scheme lets you pay a fixed % of gross turnover, potentially saving money.
statsPage.tipGB1Desc: You don't need to report up to £1,000 in sales income to HMRC annually. Above that, self-employment registration is required.
statsPage.tipGB2Desc: Deduct raw materials, shipping, stall fees, and travel expenses. Working from home allows partial deduction of household utility costs.
statsPage.tipGB3Desc: HMRC may require advance payments based on last year's tax bill. Budget ahead to avoid cash flow issues.
statsPage.tipDE0Desc: If last year's revenue was under €22,000 and this year's expected revenue is under €50,000, you may be exempt from VAT.
statsPage.tipDE1Desc: Deduct materials, shipping, booth fees, travel, and supplies as business expenses. Documentation must be kept for 10 years.
statsPage.tipDE2Desc: Regular taxpayers can deduct VAT shown on purchase invoices as input tax credit.
statsPage.tipSG0Desc: GST registration is mandatory only when taxable turnover exceeds S$1M. Below that, voluntary registration is available.
statsPage.tipSG1Desc: Take advantage of various government support schemes for tax deductions on innovation and technology investments.
statsPage.tipSG2Desc: Small businesses can receive partial tax exemption: 75% of first S$10,000, 50% of next S$190,000 of chargeable income.
